text:
alice: Quick thread — we keep hitting noisy routing edges where some mobile clients include Client-Hints (Sec-CH-UA, Sec-CH-UA-Mobile) but the X-Auth-User header is sometimes stripped by proxies. We need a deterministic priority for routing to tenant pools and quota attribution. Should gateway prefer signed auth, then Client-Hints, then User-Agent? Also: quotas per-tenant vs per-device UA variants — how aggressive do we want to be with heuristic mapping?

ben: I think priority should be: 1) verified auth (signed header / bearer) 2) client-supplied tenant claim (signed) 3) client-hint mapping 4) UA fingerprint fallback. Spoofing risk is real for UA, so treat UA as low-trust. :warning:

carla: Agreed. We should require a signature on any header that claims tenant identity (eg X-Customer-Claim and X-Claim-Sig). If signature missing, fall back to a hashed device id derived from Sec-CH-UA + Accept-Language + IP (with privacy controls). Also canonicalize headers (lowercase) at the edge to avoid dupes.

dan: Putting a config sketch here — canary patch for the gateway routing rules (pseudo-yaml):

```
route_rules:
  - name: tenant_from_signed_auth
    match:
      headers:
        - name: "x-auth-user"
          type: signed
    action: route->tenant_pool(${x-auth-user.id})
    set_trace_header: "x-routing-decision=signed-auth"

  - name: tenant_from_client_claim
    match:
      headers:
        - name: "x-customer-claim"
          type: signed
    action: route->tenant_pool(${x-customer-claim})
    set_trace_header: "x-routing-decision=claim"

  - name: tenant_from_client_hints
    match:
      headers:
        - name: "sec-ch-ua"
        - name: "sec-ch-ua-mobile"
    action: route->device_fingerprint_pool(hash(sech-ua, accept-language))
    set_trace_header: "x-routing-decision=client-hint"

  - name: fallback_ua
    match:
      headers:
        - name: "user-agent"
    action: route->anonymous_pool
    set_trace_header: "x-routing-decision=ua-fallback"
```

This also sets x-routing-decision for telemetry so we can measure hit rates.

alice: Nice. For quota attribution: if we route to anonymous_pool (no tenant), do we apply tenant-level quotas? I think we should not, and instead have device-level quotas with much lower limits so we don't have silent quota starvation for real tenants whose headers were stripped.

paula: Another option: if auth missing but a client-hint exists, create a short-lived ephemeral session token by hitting /session/claim (server-side) and return Set-Cookie. That way subsequent requests are attributed correctly. Pros: more accurate quotas. Cons: extra RTT on first request and possible abuse. We could make it opt-in via a header.

ben: Security note: Client-Hints and UA are trivially spoofable. If we accept them for routing/quota, we must pair with rate-limits and anomaly detection. Also consider requiring TLS client certs or mTLS for dedicated customers that need stronger guarantees.

carla: For telemetry/dashboarding: add counters for routing_decision (signed-auth / claim / client-hint / ua-fallback) and a gauge for "quota_attributed_as" (tenant_id | anonymous | ephemeral). Push these to the per-route dashboards so product teams can see how often fallbacks happen. Also capture a sample of headers (scrubbed) for forensics.

dan: I'll open a PR that implements the config above as a canary behind a feature flag. Plan: 1) add trace header + metrics 2) enable for 1% traffic 3) monitor for 24h 4) bump to 10% if no spikes. Anyone object?

alice: No objections. One more UX ask: can the console show the routing_decision distribution per endpoint + a link to sampled traces? That'll make rollouts so much easier to validate.

paula: Yep, we can add a per-route widget: pie chart of routing decisions + top 5 client-hint fingerprints. Will add to the backlog and prioritize after the metric is in.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary feature-flag "client-hint-routing" created by dan, targeting eng-platform:1%.

ben: Minor add: ensure we add an SLO for "no more than 0.5% of authenticated tenant traffic misrouted to anonymous_pool" during canary, otherwise rollback.

alice: Great call. dan, please include that SLO in the PR description. I'll coordinate dashboard needs with paula. :thumbsup:
